title: wt sync run|resume|undo --json
description: What a wt sync run, resume or undo did. Printed by `wt sync run [<work>...] --json`, `wt sync [<work>...] --run --json`, `wt sync resume <work> --json` and `wt sync undo <work> --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends it. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

repo.description: The main checkout, as wt sweep --json names the repository; null when the verb stopped before reading it.

onto.description: The trunk commit rebased onto: after the run's fetch, or the one the handed-over run recorded. Null for undo.

trunkSync.description: What the run did to local trunk after its fetch, as for wt up. Null when it did not fetch, and always for resume and undo.

outcome.description: done: every participant rebased, fastForwarded, undone or skipped. refused: nothing changed, or error stopped the verb first. partial: something changed and not everything finished. interrupted: a signal ended it.

error.description: Why the verb stopped before touching any participant; for undo, also why it stopped after putting some back.

recovery.description: For interrupted: the way back wt printed.

trunkSync.description: Local trunk against origin/<trunk>, and what was done about it. See docs/json.md.

local.description: Local trunk after the run (as found unless fast-forwarded); null when there is none.

remote.description: The origin/<trunk> commit compared with; null when there is none.

localAhead.description: Commits local trunk has that origin lacks, as found.

remoteAhead.description: Commits origin has that local trunk lacks, as found.

skippedReason.description: Why local trunk was left; null when fast-forwarded or with nothing to do.

result.description: rebased, fastForwarded, rebasedStepFailed, needsRecovery, handedOver, interrupted and undone changed the branch or worktree; skipped, refused, notRun and restored left them as they were. fastForwarded (since 1.2.0): the branch was behind its own remote and has nothing to rebase at the remote's commit, so the run moved it there and that is all; after is that commit, pushCommand is null, undoCommand puts it back.

pushCommand.description: For rebased: the push, as an argv.

safetyRef.description: The ref pinning the branch's tip from before the run: refs/wt-sync/<branch>/<epoch>.

deferred.description: What each deferred step of a finished rebase came to.

reason.description: Why it failed or was skipped.

undoCommand.description: What puts it back where the run found it, as an argv; null when there is nothing to undo.

planFile.description: For handedOver: the plan file saying what is yours.

ownRemoteSync.description: Since 1.2.0. Always an object from wt sync run; always null from resume and undo, which do not check: the check ran when the run started.
Since 1.2.0: what the run found of a participant's own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of its branch would replace, and what it did about it. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch; null only when no ref could be named.

state.description: As found, before anything moved; the states are those of ownRemote in wt status --json.

local.description: The branch as found, before any fast-forward: where wt sync undo puts it back.

remote.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

localAhead.description: Commits only the branch had; null for none, gone and unknown.

remoteAhead.description: Commits only the remote had; null for none, gone and unknown.

fastForwarded.description: The run moved the branch from local to remote before rebasing it. It stays true as a record when the rebase after it was put back, which takes the branch back to local.

allowed.description: state is diverged and the run went on over it under --allow-diverged; false when the participant was refused for something else.

skippedReason.description: Why the own remote refuses the participant; null when it does not. diverged: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session: behind, and it cannot be fast-forwarded. failed: the fast-forward itself did not go through; nothing of this participant was touched. fetchFailed: the branch's own remote could not be fetched, so the run could not look; trunk's fetch failing is the run's error instead.
